summary: Kubernetes readiness probes in private VPC counting against tenant quota and triggering 429s during scale-up
description: Issue summary: NimbusDocs reported sudden 429s after a scheduled autoscaler rollout on their Private VPC deployment. Impact: Customer-facing inference requests returned 429s for ~18 minutes during a scale-up window, causing failed background jobs and degradation of customer experience. Observed behavior: Spikes in small GET/POST requests originating from K8s readiness probes across newly created pods. Probes used the same mounted API key and hit the normal /v1/chat/completions endpoint. Those probe requests were counted against tenant token quota and correlated with the 429s. This appears limited to the Private deployment (VPC) path where probe traffic traversed the ingress sidecar and was not exempted from quota accounting.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a private/redwood inference client inside a k8s cluster using NimbusDocs helm chart (example manifest attached in ticket).
2) Configure readinessProbe to call /v1/health/check or (mis)configured to call /v1/chat/completions with an API key mounted in the pod (interval 5s, failureThreshold 3).
3) Scale deployment from 2 -> 25 pods to force parallel readiness checks during startup.
4) Observe per-tenant token usage in Redwood Console and watch for 429s returned to real traffic during the scale-up period.

2026-03-11T09:12:04Z rate-limiter WARN token_bucket_exhausted tenant=acct-nimbus-01 window=60s remaining=0
2026-03-11T09:12:05Z serving-runtime ERROR response=429 tenant=acct-nimbus-01 route=/v1/chat/completions request_id=abc123
2026-03-11T09:25:30Z support NOTE observed repeated small payloads (~80-150B) from 10.0.12.* (k8s node CIDR) matching pod readinessProbe pattern
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: bursty client traffic during scale-up exceeded tenant burst credits.

Found evidence: readinessProbe target was the normal API path and used the customer API key; probe frequency (5s across 20 new pods) produced ~240 probe requests in the first 2 minutes — enough to exhaust short-window burst budget.
Private deployment detail: ingress sidecar does not currently exempt cluster-local IP ranges from quota accounting by default — probe traffic went through normal quota pipeline.
Checked console graphs: token rate spike aligns exactly with pod creation timestamps and K8s events (autoscaler).
Cross-checked with SRE: no global rate-limiter or outage; this is tenant-level exhaustion accounting.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-11: Reproduced pattern in staging by spinning up 15 pods with readinessProbe hitting /v1/chat/completions. Confirmed quota drop and 429s for normal traffic during warmup.
Carlos Mendez (SRE) 2026-03-11: Noted that our private ingress honors X-Forwarded-For but still attributes quota by API key. We need a safe exclusion for k8s node IPs or an internal health endpoint.

NimbusDocs (Customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed they mounted the API key into the container for app-level checks; they used the same probe path for convenience. Asking for immediate mitigation while they update manifests.
Support (Aisha) 2026-03-12: Suggested temporary workaround below and requested console timestamps / example pod names from customer to correlate.
root_cause: Kubernetes readiness/liveness probes were configured to hit billing-counted inference endpoints using a tenant API key. During a rapid scale-up the aggregated probes consumed the tenant's short-window burst credits and triggered 429 throttles for legitimate traffic.
workaround: Immediate customer action: change readiness/liveness probes to either (a) call a local/read-only health endpoint (127.0.0.1:<port>/health) that does not traverse the public API, or (b) reduce probe frequency/failureThreshold during autoscale windows. Support action: temporarily create an internal 'probe-exempt' API key for NimbusDocs on the Private control plane and mark probe-origin IP CIDR as exempt (safety-limited; revoke after manifest update).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 10:10 UTC: Created temporary probe-exempt key scoped to internal IP CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 — confirmed immediate drop in probe-request accounting and 429s cleared.
Customer updated helm chart to use local health endpoint and removed API key from readinessProbe. Validated scale-up without 429s in post-change test.
SRE action item: recommend adding an ingress config option for private deployments to define 'internal-health-cidrs' that are excluded from quota accounting (PR opened).
follow_up_tasks: INT-3982: Add 'internal-health-cidrs' config to Private ingress and document behavior (owner: Carlos).
Support KB: Publish article with k8s probe examples and a checklist for Private deployments (owner: Aisha).
Security review: probe-exempt keys process to ensure least privilege and auditing (owner: Priya Rao).
suggested_config_changes: For customers: never point readiness/liveness to billing-counted endpoints. Use container-local endpoints or admin-only paths that are excluded from usage accounting.
For platform: expose an opt-in Private-deploy config to whitelist CIDRs or service account IDs for quota exclusion, and log when probe-exempt policy is used.
For console: surface per-key short-window peak graphs and an alert when short-window consumption exceeds X% of burst credit during scale events.
